archetypes.name: Limits to Growth
archetypes.story: A reinforcing growth loop hits a balancing constraint it never planned for; effort accelerates while results plateau.
archetypes.diagnosis: Find the constraining loop — a resource, a market, a skill, a rate limiter — that strengthens as you grow. Growth loops never stall on their own; something is balancing them.
archetypes.intervention: Weaken or remove the constraint BEFORE pushing the growth loop harder. If the constraint is structural (market size), change the system's goal or market, not the effort.
archetypes.counterintuitive: Pushing the growth loop harder tightens the constraint faster. Ease off, remove the limiter, then resume.

archetypes.name: Shifting the Burden
archetypes.story: A symptomatic fix works fast and erodes the pressure to find the fundamental fix; reliance on the quick fix grows its own constituency.
archetypes.diagnosis: Two balancing loops attack the same problem symptom: one fast-and-shallow (with side effects), one slow-and-deep. Track whether the deep solution's attention/investment is declining.
archetypes.intervention: Apply the fundamental fix while using the symptomatic fix ONLY as a explicitly-time-boxed bridge. Make the side effect of the quick fix visible and costly to its owner.
archetypes.counterintuitive: The quick fix's success is the disease. Each painless relief lowers the motivation to solve the real problem.

archetypes.name: Eroding Goals (Drifting Goals)
archetypes.story: A gap between goal and performance gets closed by lowering the goal instead of raising performance.
archetypes.diagnosis: Compare the goal's written value over time. If it drifts down (or the metric's definition loosens) whenever performance lags, the loop is goal-erosion, not effort failure.
archetypes.intervention: Pin the goal externally — contract, public commitment, automatic escalation on miss. Separate 'goal' from 'forecast': the goal may not follow performance.
archetypes.counterintuitive: Adjusting the goal to match reality feels pragmatic; it is the system quietly deleting its own ambition.

archetypes.name: Fixes That Fail
archetypes.story: A fix works now, creates an unintended consequence that regenerates the original problem — often after a delay long enough to hide the causal link.
archetypes.diagnosis: Map the fix → side-effect → problem loop with its delay. Ask: what does this fix make CHEAPER that should stay expensive?
archetypes.intervention: If the fix is unavoidable, plan its removal at birth (sunset clause) and instrument the delayed consequence. Prefer fixes that don't feed the problem loop at all.
archetypes.counterintuitive: The fix is working — that is exactly why the problem persists.

archetypes.name: Tragedy of the Commons
archetypes.story: Individual actors rationally consume a shared finite resource until it collapses for all.
archetypes.diagnosis: Identify the commons (budget, attention, compute, calendar, brand, a shared codebase) and check whether individual gain and collective cost are measured by different ledgers.
archetypes.intervention: Make the resource's cost visible at point of use (metering, chargeback), divide the commons, or set hard allocation rules with enforcement — appeals to restraint alone fail.
archetypes.counterintuitive: Each actor is behaving rationally; the structure is irrational. Fix structure, not people.

archetypes.name: Growth and Underinvestment
archetypes.story: Demand grows, capacity investment lags because performance looks 'not yet bad enough', degraded performance then suppresses demand, justifying the underinvestment — a self-fulfilling stall.
symptoms: we will invest when demand proves it
archetypes.diagnosis: Check the order of events: did demand fall BECAUSE capacity was starved? If performance decline precedes demand decline, the market is not rejecting you — your underinvestment is.
archetypes.intervention: Invest ahead of demand based on the growth loop's potential, not current utilization. Build capacity BEFORE the signal confirms it (the confirming signal never comes).
archetypes.counterintuitive: Waiting for proof of demand manufactures the evidence for not investing.

archetypes.name: Success to the Successful
archetypes.story: Two competitors for one resource pool; the early winner gets more resource, widening the gap regardless of merit.
archetypes.diagnosis: Trace the allocation rule. If allocation correlates with past success rather than marginal return, the loop compounds initial advantage into permanent dominance.
archetypes.intervention: Change the allocation rule to marginal-return or rotation. Split resource pools. If the dominance IS the strategy, name it; do not pretend it is meritocracy.
archetypes.counterintuitive: The allocation often looks fair (performance-based) while being the engine of the imbalance.

archetypes.name: Escalation
archetypes.story: Two balancing-from-one-side loops mirror each other: A's advantage threatens B, B responds, A responds — spending rises while relative position stays flat.
archetypes.diagnosis: Find the two symmetric reinforcing loops and the shared 'relative position' stock. Ask what single dimension the escalation is measured on.
archetypes.intervention: Refuse the dimension: compete where the other party cannot or will not respond (asymmetry), or convert the zero-sum stock into a positive-sum one (grow the market, standardize).
archetypes.counterintuitive: Unilateral de-escalation loses only if the shared dimension is truly fixed — it almost never is.

archetypes.name: Policy Resistance
archetypes.story: Every stakeholder pulls the system state toward their preferred level; the net of all the pulls keeps the state stubbornly where it was despite repeated interventions.
archetypes.diagnosis: Inventory the actors and each one's pull (their balancing loop toward their goal). Your policy is one more pull, matched by counter-pulls you funded.
archetypes.intervention: Find where the actors' goals can align (shared stock or metric), or reduce the power of the strongest opposing pull, or let go of the state and move the goal — never just push harder.
archetypes.counterintuitive: The system is not stuck despite everyone's effort; it is stuck BECAUSE of everyone's effort.

archetypes.name: Addiction (Shifting-the-Burden variant)
archetypes.story: An external agent absorbs a symptom, the internal capability atrophies, and withdrawal becomes impossible even when the external agent's cost explodes.
archetypes.diagnosis: Check capability trends on the internal fundamental loop. Addiction = Shifting-the-Burden where the quick fix is owned by an external party whose incentives diverge.
archetypes.intervention: Rebuild internal capability in parallel while still using the external fix; taper on a schedule, not on pain. Price the dependency (switching cost) quarterly to keep it visible.
archetypes.counterintuitive: The external fix's quality is irrelevant — even a perfect fix deepens the atrophy.
